question: I have an Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass and I just moved to a new apartment last week. How soon do I need to update MOM with my new address, and how do I do it?
expected_answer: You need to update MOM within 2 weeks of changing your residential address. Otherwise, you may be penalised. To update: (1) Ensure that your new address meets the relevant housing requirements. (2) Log in to EP eService to update your address. The update is immediate. (3) Print the acknowledgement page and keep it with your pass card.
actual_answer:
You need to update MOM **within 2 weeks** of changing your residential address [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/notify-mom/index.md].

Here's how to update your address:

1. Ensure your new address meets the relevant [housing requirements](https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-worker/housing/various-types-of-housing)
2. Log in to [EP eService](https://www.mom.gov.sg/eservices/services/employment-pass-eservice) to update your address — the update is immediate
3. Print the acknowledgement page and keep it with your pass card

[source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/notify-mom/index.md]

If you don't update within 2 weeks, you may be penalized [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/notify-mom/index.md].

question: We have an EP holder on an EP (Sponsorship) whose pass is expiring soon. I want to make sure I submit the renewal in time — how early can I start the renewal, and how long should I expect processing to take? Also, once we get the IPA letter, how long is it valid for?
expected_answer: For EP (Sponsorship), you can start applying to renew 3 months before the pass expires (as opposed to the standard EP, which allows renewal up to 6 months / 180 days before expiry). You must apply before the expiry date. Processing time for EP (Sponsorship) renewals is within 6 weeks for most cases (the renewal form itself states around 8 weeks). Once the renewal is approved, you will receive an in-principle approval (IPA) letter that is valid for 3 months. You must get the pass issued before the IPA or the current pass expires, whichever occurs first — otherwise an overstaying fine will be imposed. The duration of the renewed pass will start when the current pass expires. Any remaining validity from the current pass (up to six months) is added on to the renewal, so renewing early does not reduce or lose validity. The renewed pass can be granted for up to 3 years.

**When you can start renewing:**

**Processing time:**
- It takes **around 8 weeks** (or within 6 weeks for most cases) to process the renewal application [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/renew-a-pass/ep_sponsor_renewal_form.md § Page 1, www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/renew-a-pass/index.md § Renew an Employment Pass]

**IPA validity:**
- Once your renewal is successful, the In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter is valid for **3 months** [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/renew-a-pass/index.md § Upon renewal]

**Important reminder:** You must get the pass issued before either the IPA or current pass expires (whichever comes first), otherwise an overstaying fine will be imposed [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/renew-a-pass/index.md § Upon renewal].

question: I'm looking into the Employment Pass for a candidate we want to hire in Singapore. What's the minimum salary needed to qualify?
expected_answer: The qualifying salary for an Employment Pass is a fixed monthly salary comparable to the top one-third of local PMET salaries. It starts from $5,600 and increases progressively with age, up to $10,700 for candidates in their mid-40s. Candidates in the financial services sector need higher salaries than these amounts to qualify. The actual value varies with age and sector of employment.
actual_answer:
The minimum salary needed to qualify for an Employment Pass depends on the candidate's **age** and **sector**:

## Current Requirements (before 1 Jan 2027):

**For most sectors:**
- Starts at **$5,600** per month for candidates aged 23 or below
- Increases progressively with age up to **$10,700** per month for those aged 45 and above

**For financial services sector:**
- Starts at **$6,200** per month for candidates aged 23 or below
- Increases progressively with age up to **$11,800** per month for those aged 45 and above

## Future Requirements (from 1 Jan 2027 for new applications):

**For most sectors:**
- Starts at **$6,000** per month (age 23 or below)
- Increases up to **$11,500** per month (age 45+)

**For financial services sector:**
- Starts at **$6,600** per month (age 23 or below)
- Increases up to **$12,700** per month (age 45+)

[source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]

**Important:** Meeting the salary requirement is only Stage 1 of eligibility. Unless exempted, candidates must also pass the points-based COMPASS assessment (Stage 2), earning at least 40 points to qualify for an EP. [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]

question: We have a candidate who's been approved for an ONE Pass. His common-law partner wants to come along and eventually work here. What type of pass does the common-law spouse get, and can they work in Singapore on that pass?
expected_answer: A common-law spouse (defined as a common-law relationship between 2 people that is recognised under the laws of their country or region) of an Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass holder is eligible for a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP). Common-law spouses on LTVP can apply for a Letter of Consent (LOC) to work in Singapore.
actual_answer:
Based on the knowledge base, here's what applies to the common-law spouse of an Overseas Networks & Expertise (ONE) Pass holder:

**Pass Type:**
- The common-law spouse is eligible for a **Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)** [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/passes-for-families/index.md]

**Working in Singapore:**
- Yes, common-law spouses on LTVP **can work in Singapore** with a **Letter of Consent (LOC)** [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/passes-for-families/index.md]

**How to Apply for the LOC:**
The prospective employer must:
1. Download and complete the Letter of Consent (Common-Law Spouse) application form
2. Submit the application form with relevant supporting documents online [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/passes-for-families/long-term-visit-pass-for-overseas-networks-expertise-pass/working-in-singapore/index.md]

**Important Note:**
The common-law relationship must be recognized under the laws of their country or region [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/passes-for-families/index.md]

question: I'm an employer planning to apply for an Employment Pass for a candidate. How long does it take to process the application, and how much is the application fee?
expected_answer: The processing time and fee depend on whether the employer has a Singapore-registered company or not. For employers with a Singapore-registered company applying online via the EP eService, the application is processed or given an update within 10 business days, and the application fee is $105, payable by GIRO, Visa, Mastercard, or Amex. For overseas companies without a Singapore-registered company (sponsorship cases), a local sponsor must submit the application, the processing time is within 6 weeks for most cases (some cases may take longer), and the application fee is also $105, payable by PayNow, Visa, Mastercard, or Amex. In either case, if additional information or documents are required, the processing time may take longer than the stated timeframes.

**Processing Time:**
- **Standard applications**: Processed or given an update within **10 business days** [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/apply-for-a-pass/index.md]
- **For overseas companies without a Singapore-registered company**: Within **6 weeks** for most cases [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/apply-for-a-pass/index.md]

**Application Fee:**
- **$105** (payable by GIRO, Visa, Mastercard, or Amex) [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/apply-for-a-pass/index.md]

**Important notes:**
- You can check your application status online after 10 business days (or 6 weeks for overseas companies)
- If additional information or documents are required, processing may take longer than the standard timeframe

question: We have a candidate who wants to apply for the ONE Pass, but our company is not publicly listed. Can we use our company valuation to qualify as an established company, or is there another way for non-listed companies to meet the criteria?
expected_answer: No, company valuation is not accepted as an alternative to market capitalisation. Non-publicly listed companies must meet the annual revenue criterion of at least US$200 million to be considered established companies, as they do not have market capitalisation. If the prospective employer does not meet the established company criteria, the candidate may still apply for the Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass after earning a fixed monthly salary of at least S$30,000 for the 12 consecutive months leading up to the date of application. Alternatively, the candidate may apply for another work pass such as the Employment Pass, Personalised Employment Pass, EntrePass, or Tech.Pass.
actual_answer:
Based on the knowledge base, **no, you cannot use company valuation** to qualify as an established company for the Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass (ONE Pass). [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/faq/one-pass/can-a-non-publicly-listed-company-be-considered-established-based-on-company-valuation.md]

For non-publicly listed companies to be considered "established," they must meet the **annual revenue criterion of at least US$200 million**, since they do not have market capitalisation. [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/faq/one-pass/can-a-non-publicly-listed-company-be-considered-established-based-on-company-valuation.md]

**Alternative options if your company doesn't meet this criterion:**

- Your candidate could apply for the ONE Pass based on having **earned a fixed monthly salary of at least S$30,000 for 12 consecutive months** with an established company (either overseas or in Singapore) [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/eligibility.md]

- If your company doesn't qualify as established, your candidate may consider applying for other work passes such as the **Employment Pass, Personalised Employment Pass, EntrePass, or Tech.Pass** [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/faq/one-pass/does-my-prospective-employer-need-to-meet-the-criteria-for-an-established-company.md]

question: We're applying for an Employment Pass for a candidate whose qualification verification through a background screening company has been pending for over two weeks. The candidate's university is one of the institutions listed in the application form's drop-down list. Do we have to wait for the verification to come back before we can submit the EP application, or is there some workaround?

Once the work pass application is approved, you can bring in the candidate and get their pass issued. You do not need to submit the verification proof to MOM after that. However, if the qualification is found to be false, the work pass will be revoked and the candidate must leave Singapore.

Based on the knowledge base, you **do not have to wait** for the verification to complete. There is a workaround available:

If your verification is still pending **after 14 working days** and the awarding institution **is from the application form's drop-down list** of accredited institutions, you can **submit the receipt for the verification service** in lieu of the actual verification proof in your work pass application [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/documents-required/bsc-guide.md].

**Key points:**

- You can proceed with the EP application using just the receipt from the background screening company
- Once the work pass application is approved, you can bring in the candidate and get their pass issued
- You do not need to submit the verification proof to MOM later
- However, be aware that if the qualification is subsequently found to be false, the work pass will be revoked and the candidate must leave Singapore

Since your candidate's university is on the accredited list and it's been over two weeks, you should be able to use this option to move forward with the application without further delay.

question: We have a candidate who earned S$30,000/month overseas for the past 12 months at a company with annual revenue of US$180 million and market cap of US$450 million. The company's global offices combined have annual revenue exceeding US$200 million though. Does the company qualify as established, and what documents do we need to submit for this candidate?
expected_answer:
For a company to be considered established, it must have at least one of the following: market capitalisation of at least US$500 million, or annual revenue of at least US$200 million. Combined amounts from the entire global office can also be considered and will be assessed on a case-by-case basis. So while the individual office does not meet either threshold on its own, the combined global revenue exceeding US$200 million may qualify, but this will be assessed case-by-case by MOM.

For a candidate whose current or last held employment was overseas, the following documents are required:
1. Passport page (including any amendments). If the candidate's name in their passport differs from their name in other documents, an explanation letter and supporting documents such as a deed poll are also needed.
2. Monthly payslips for the 12 consecutive months leading up to the date of application.
3. Employment verification proof from a background screening company.
4. Documents supporting other income sources other than fixed monthly salary (if applicable).
5. Latest financial information of the candidate's employer obtained within the last 3 months, including documents indicating the latest market capitalisation or annual company revenue. If this information is not available, the company's latest audited Profit & Loss statements may be provided instead. MOM will only consider documents from third party auditors; documents signed by the company's management staff will not be accepted.

Additionally, if the candidate drew salaries from more than one employer in the 12 consecutive months leading up to the date of application, the qualifying fixed monthly salary of at least S$30,000 (or its equivalent in foreign currency) should come from one employer only. Other sources of income may be considered on a case-by-case basis.
actual_answer:
Based on the information provided, **yes, the company can qualify as established** for the Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass application, but it requires case-by-case assessment.

Here's why:

While the individual office doesn't meet the standalone thresholds (US$500 million market cap OR US$200 million annual revenue), **combined amounts from the entire global office can be considered** [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/eligibility.md]. Since you mention the global offices combined exceed US$200 million in annual revenue, this should qualify.

## Documents Required

For a candidate with **current or last held employment overseas**, you need to submit:

- **Passport page**, including any amendments
- **Monthly payslips** for the 12 consecutive months leading up to the date of application
- **Employment verification proof** from a background screening company
- **Documents supporting other income sources** (if applicable, beyond fixed monthly salary)
- **Latest financial information** of the employer obtained within the last 3 months, showing:
  - Latest market capitalisation OR annual company revenue
  - This can come from sources like Bloomberg, Reuters, or company annual reports
  - **Important**: Since you're relying on combined global revenue, ensure the financial documents clearly show the global consolidated figures

If the above financial information isn't available, you may provide the company's latest audited Profit & Loss statements from third-party auditors [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/documents-required.md].

question: My company is lowering the salary of one of our EP holders. How far in advance do we need to notify MOM, and what happens if the new salary doesn't meet the qualifying threshold?
expected_answer: As an employer, you must submit a request to MOM at least 1 month before the date you intend to lower the salary. The pass holder must continue to qualify for the work pass they are holding with the revised salary. You may use the Self-Assessment Tool (SAT) to find out if they are likely to meet the qualifying salary. If they do not qualify with the revised salary, you should cancel the work pass and apply for a new work pass based on the pass holder's eligibility.

**Notification Timeline:**
- You must submit a request **at least 1 month before** the date you intend to lower the salary [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/notify-mom-of-changes/index.md]

- The pass holder must continue to qualify for the Employment Pass with the revised salary

question: We're a high-growth startup incorporated in Singapore and we want to know if we can qualify for the SEP bonus under COMPASS. We've raised about USD 12 million over the last 3 years from a VC that isn't EDBI or SEEDS Capital. Does that count, or does the funding have to come from specific investors?
expected_answer: High-growth startups incorporated in Singapore can qualify for the SEP bonus if they have a minimum investment amount of USD 10 million over the past 36 months. The funding must have been received from EDBI, SEEDS Capital, or other recognised investment firms (there is a separate list of recognised investment firms maintained for this purpose). So your startup would meet the investment threshold (USD 12 million exceeds the USD 10 million minimum) and the 36-month timeframe, but the VC firm you received funding from must be on the list of recognised investment firms. If it is not EDBI or SEEDS Capital, it needs to be one of the other firms on that recognised list. This programme is supported by Enterprise Singapore (EnterpriseSG), and you can contact them at ENTERPRISESG_COMPASS@enterprisesg.gov.sg for queries, including whether your investor qualifies.
actual_answer:
Based on the knowledge base, to qualify for the SEP bonus as a high-growth startup, your company must meet **all** of the following criteria:

- Be incorporated in Singapore
- Have a minimum investment amount of **USD $10 million** over the past 36 months
- Have received funding from **EDBI, SEEDS Capital, or other recognised investment firms**

Since you've raised USD $12 million over the last 3 years and are incorporated in Singapore, you meet the first two requirements. [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/compass-c6-strategic-economic-priorities-sep-bonus-eligible-programmes/annex-c---eligible-programmes-for-sep-bonus.md]

**Regarding your VC investor:** The program does allow funding from "other recognised investment firms" beyond just EDBI and SEEDS Capital. However, the knowledge base doesn't specify which investment firms are considered "recognised." 

**Next steps:** You should contact **Enterprise Singapore (EnterpriseSG)** directly at **ENTERPRISESG_COMPASS@enterprisesg.gov.sg** to confirm whether your VC investor qualifies as a "recognised investment firm" for the SEP bonus program. [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/compass-c6-strategic-economic-priorities-sep-bonus-eligible-programmes/index.md]

The award of the SEP bonus is at the discretion of the supporting agencies (in this case, EnterpriseSG), and if approved, MOM will notify your organization and the points will be reflected in the Self-Assessment Tool. [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]

These benchmarks were released in August 2025 and are updated once a year to reflect the latest market conditions. The required salary increases progressively with age, from age 23 to age 45. **To score points under C1:**

- **10 points**: The candidate's fixed monthly salary must meet or exceed the **65th percentile** of local PMET salaries in the financial services sector for their age (30)
- **20 points (maximum)**: The salary must reach the **90th percentile or above** for the sector and age [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]

The exact salary figures are published in sector-specific benchmark documents that are updated annually. question: I have an EP holder working for us who does manual labour. Do I need to buy medical insurance or work injury compensation insurance for them? I'm confused about what's actually required for EP holders versus other pass types.
expected_answer:
Providing medical insurance is not a requirement for employing Employment Pass (EP) holders. Most EP holders may already have their own medical insurance or may want to choose their own coverage. For EP holders without existing medical insurance, employers can choose to provide insurance coverage as part of the employment contract, or encourage them to get their own. The medical insurance requirement applies only to Work Permit and S Pass holders, in line with employers' existing responsibility for the upkeep and maintenance of their migrant workers, including the provision of medical treatment.

However, for work injury compensation (WIC) insurance, buying it is only mandatory if you are employing manual workers or non-manual workers earning less than $1,600 a month. So if your EP holder is a manual worker, you are required to purchase work injury compensation insurance for them. Whether or not you have purchased WIC insurance, you are still required to pay compensation for an eligible claim.

Additionally, under the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA), you are obligated to pay any eligible claims for workplace injuries. You are also obligated to provide paid sick leave, including dental leave, to any employee covered under the Employment Act.

Based on the knowledge base, here's what you need to know about insurance requirements for your Employment Pass (EP) holder who does manual labor:

**Medical Insurance: NOT required**
- Providing medical insurance is not mandatory for EP holders [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/faq/employment-pass/are-employers-required-to-buy-medical-insurance-for-employment-pass-holders.md]
- You can choose to provide it as part of the employment contract or encourage them to get their own coverage [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/faq/employment-pass/are-employers-required-to-buy-medical-insurance-for-employment-pass-holders.md]

**Work Injury Compensation (WIC) Insurance: REQUIRED for your case**
- Since your EP holder is a manual worker, you ARE required to purchase work injury compensation insurance for them [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/faq/employment-pass/what-are-my-medical-obligations-as-the-employer-of-an-ep-holder.md]
- Generally, WIC insurance is only mandatory for manual workers or non-manual workers earning less than $1,600/month [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/faq/employment-pass/does-an-employer-need-to-buy-wic-insurance-for-an-ep-holder.md]

**Other obligations:**
- You must provide paid sick leave (including dental leave) if covered under the Employment Act [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/faq/employment-pass/what-are-my-medical-obligations-as-the-employer-of-an-ep-holder.md]
- You're obligated to pay eligible claims for workplace injuries under WICA, regardless of whether you have insurance [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/faq/employment-pass/does-an-employer-need-to-buy-wic-insurance-for-an-ep-holder.md]

question: We have a candidate who's currently on a Dependant's Pass under an Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass holder — not the spouse, just a dependent. They want to work for us. Can they just get a Letter of Consent like spouses do, or do they need a separate work pass?
expected_answer: Only spouses of Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass holders can work or operate a business in Singapore with a Letter of Consent (LOC). Other dependants who are not spouses will need to obtain a work pass to work for an employer in Singapore. If the dependant obtains an EP or S Pass, they will be granted the work and stay privileges associated with that pass, their stay will no longer depend on the main Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass holder, and they will need to cancel their Dependant's Pass before the EP or S Pass is issued. If the dependant obtains a Work Permit instead, they must hold on to both the Work Permit and the Dependant's Pass; the Work Permit validity will be tied to the DP's validity; they can apply for any Work Permit regardless of nationality or citizenship; they are not subject to the six-monthly medical examination, security bond, or pregnancy restrictions; and they do not need medical insurance from the employer if they are already covered under a medical insurance plan that meets MOM's prevailing minimum mandatory insurance coverage requirement.
actual_answer:
Based on the knowledge base, **they need a separate work pass** — they cannot get a Letter of Consent.

Only **spouses** of Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass holders can work in Singapore using a Letter of Consent (LOC). Other dependants who are not spouses must obtain a regular work pass (Employment Pass, S Pass, or Work Permit) to work for an employer [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/passes-for-families/dependants-pass-for-overseas-networks-expertise-pass/working-in-singapore.md].

question: We're putting together an EP application for a candidate who's 30 years old for our technology consultancy company. I want to understand the COMPASS salary benchmarks — what fixed monthly salary do we need to hit for the C1 criterion to score points, and what's the difference between the 10-point and 20-point thresholds at that age?
expected_answer: For a candidate aged 30, the required salary for 10 COMPASS points (which corresponds to the 65th percentile of local PMETs in ICT, information communication technology sector) is $8,971 , and the required salary for 20 points (the 90th percentile of local PMETs in ICT ) is $13,959. The difference between the two thresholds at age 30 is $4,988.
actual_answer:
Based on the knowledge base, here's what you need to know about the C1 Salary criterion for COMPASS:

**How C1 Salary scoring works:**

- **10 points**: Candidate's fixed monthly salary falls between the **65th to less than 90th percentile** of local PMET salaries in your sector
- **20 points**: Candidate's fixed monthly salary is at or above the **90th percentile** of local PMET salaries in your sector
- **0 points**: Below the 65th percentile

[source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]

**Important notes:**

1. The C1 Salary criterion is **different from the EP qualifying salary**. Even if your candidate scores points under C1, they must still meet the minimum EP qualifying salary to be eligible for an EP. [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/compass-booklet.md]

2. The specific salary benchmarks vary by **sector** and **age**. The benchmarks increase progressively from age 23 to age 45. [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/compass-c1-salary-benchmarks/index.md]

3. You can download the actual C1 salary benchmark figures by sector from MOM's website, which are updated annually. [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/compass-c1-salary-benchmarks/index.md]

To get the exact salary thresholds for a 30-year-old in the technology consultancy sector, you'll need to check your organization's specific sector classification and refer to the downloadable C1 salary benchmarks document.

question: We're hiring someone who currently holds a Dependant's Pass tied to an ONE Pass holder. She'll be coming on board on a Work Permit. Her current medical insurance already meets MOM's minimum mandatory coverage requirement. Do we still need to provide her with medical insurance, and are there any other sector-specific requirements she'd be exempt from?
expected_answer: If the DP holder already has medical insurance that meets MOM's prevailing minimum mandatory insurance coverage requirement, the employer does not need to provide medical insurance. In addition, a DP holder (tied to an ONE Pass) working on a Work Permit is exempt from the six-monthly medical examination, the security bond requirement, and pregnancy restrictions. There are also no nationality or citizenship restrictions on the Work Permit application, and the Work Permit validity will be tied to the DP's validity.
actual_answer:
Based on the knowledge base, **you do not need to provide separate medical insurance** for this employee, as long as her existing medical insurance already meets MOM's prevailing minimum mandatory insurance coverage requirement and covers the full period of the Work Permit validity [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-worker/sector-specific-rules/medical-insurance/index.md].

Additionally, as a Dependant's Pass holder of an ONE Pass (Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass) holder who obtains a Work Permit, she will be **exempt from several other sector-specific requirements**:

• **Six-monthly medical examination** – not required  
• **Security bond** – not required  
• **Pregnancy restrictions** – not applicable  

[source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/passes-for-families/dependants-pass-for-overseas-networks-expertise-pass/working-in-singapore.md]

**Important note:** She will need to hold on to both her Work Permit and her Dependant's Pass for the ONE Pass holder. Her Work Permit validity will be tied to her Dependant's Pass validity [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/passes-for-families/dependants-pass-for-overseas-networks-expertise-pass/working-in-singapore.md].

question: We're looking to hire a foreign specialist for a role that's on the Shortage Occupation List. Our candidate graduated from KU Leuven in Belgium. When we submit the EP application, do we just pick any job title, or is there a specific process we need to follow for the SOL role — and will the candidate's university help with the application?
expected_answer: For a Shortage Occupation List (SOL) role, the SOL bonus recognises jobs requiring highly specialised skills that are in shortage in the local workforce, determined through a robust evaluation process considering industry needs and local workforce development efforts. To qualify for this bonus: (1) the candidate must perform the job duties listed for the specific shortage occupation; (2) you must select one of the eligible job titles in the EP application (not just any title); and (3) the candidate must meet checks on additional job requirements if they fall into certain categories. Regarding the candidate's university, Katholieke Universiteit Leuven (KU Leuven) in Belgium is on the list of recognised institutions, which can support the EP application (e.g., for meeting qualification-related criteria). So the university credential from KU Leuven is recognised, but you still need to follow the specific SOL application requirements including selecting the correct eligible job title and ensuring the candidate meets the relevant job duty and additional requirement checks.
actual_answer:
Based on the knowledge base, here's what you need to do for a Shortage Occupation List (SOL) role:

**Job Title Selection:**
- You must select one of the **eligible job titles** listed for the specific shortage occupation in your EP application form [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/compass-c5-skills-bonus-shortage-occupation-list-sol/index.md]
- This job title must match the occupation you advertised on MyCareersFuture, unless you're exempted from the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) job advertising requirement [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/compass-c5-skills-bonus-shortage-occupation-list-sol/index.md]

**Application Requirements:**
To obtain the C5 Skills bonus points, you need to:
1. Ensure your candidate performs the job duties listed for the specific shortage occupation
2. Select the shortage occupation in your EP application
3. Meet any additional requirements specific to that occupation (such as relevant qualifications, work experience, or registration proof) [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]

**University's Role:**
The candidate's university (KU Leuven) does not help with the application. You, as the employer, submit the EP application and upload the candidate's qualifications in the qualifications section of the EP application form [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/compass-c5-skills-bonus-shortage-occupation-list-sol/sol-guidebook.md]

For the Software Development Manager role, the candidate can qualify for the C5 Skills Bonus on the Shortage Occupation List even without a relevant degree, because the additional requirements allow either (1a) at least a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Programming & Systems Analysis, or Science (Computer Studies), OR (1b) a minimum total of three years' work experience in at least one of the eligible job titles (Application development manager, Head of applications development, Software and applications manager, or Software development manager). Since your candidate has four years of experience as a Software Development Manager, he satisfies criterion (1b) and would be eligible. The supporting agency is IMDA.

For the Relationship Manager (ultra-high/high net worth / family office / philanthropy) role, the candidate would NOT qualify. The additional requirements for that role require the candidate to meet BOTH criteria: (1) the employer must be a Singapore licensed FI with private banking business (which your firm satisfies — MOM verifies this directly with MAS, no additional documentation needed), AND (2) the candidate must have a minimum total of three years' work experience as a Relationship Manager (ultra-high/high net worth / family office / philanthropy). Your candidate has only two years of experience, which falls short of the three-year minimum. The supporting agency is MAS.

So only the Software Development Manager candidate would qualify; the Relationship Manager candidate would not.
actual_answer:
Based on the Shortage Occupation List (SOL) requirements, here's how each candidate stands:

**Software Development Manager candidate: Does NOT qualify**

The SOL requires candidates to meet **either** criterion (1a) or (1b):
- (1a) At least a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Programming & Systems Analysis, or Science (Computer Studies)
- (1b) Minimum total **three years'** work experience as a Software Development Manager (or related titles)

Your candidate has four years of experience, which exceeds the three-year threshold under criterion (1b). However, his mechanical engineering degree does not satisfy criterion (1a). Since he meets criterion (1b) through his four years of relevant experience, **he would qualify** for the Skills Bonus. [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/compass-c5-skills-bonus-shortage-occupation-list-sol/index.md]

1. Employer is a Singapore licensed FI with private banking business (your firm meets this)
2. Minimum total **three years'** work experience as a Relationship Manager (ultra-high/high net worth / family office / philanthropy)

Your candidate has only two years of experience, falling short of the required three years. Therefore, **this candidate does not qualify** for the Skills Bonus under the SOL. question: I'm a researcher considering applying for the Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass. I know it covers multiple sectors, but I'm not sure how the eligibility assessment works — do I just need to meet some general criteria, or is it more specific than that? And what kind of employer-related financial documents would I need to prepare, and how recent do they have to be?
expected_answer: The Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass covers top talent in all sectors, including academia and research, so you would be eligible to apply as a researcher. For eligibility, candidates are assessed on a case-by-case basis. You must choose the category that best fits you and meet all the criteria within that chosen category — not just some general criteria. Regarding employer-related financial documents, you need to provide the latest financial information of your employer, obtained within the last 3 months. This includes documents indicating the latest market capitalisation or annual company revenue. Additionally, if you have income sources other than your fixed monthly salary, you must provide documents supporting those other income sources. You will also need employment verification proof from a background screening company.
actual_answer:
Based on the knowledge base, here's how the eligibility assessment works for researchers:

## Assessment Approach

**Sector-Specific Evaluation**: If you're applying as a researcher, you would qualify under the "outstanding achievements" track in **academia and research** [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/eligibility.md]. This allows you to apply *without* meeting the salary criteria. MOM and other agencies (including MOE, NRF, and A*STAR) will holistically review your application based on your work and key achievements [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/eligibility.md].

**Case-by-Case Assessment**: All Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass candidates are assessed on a case-by-case basis [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/eligibility.md].

## Employer Financial Documents

If you're *not* applying under outstanding achievements and instead need to meet the salary criteria, here's what's relevant:

- **For overseas employment**: Your employer must be an "established company" with either:
  - Market capitalisation of at least US$500 million, OR

question: My company is terminating an EP holder and their last day is 15 February. We want to submit the cancellation early, and we also want to make sure the person can stay in Singapore for a while after the pass is cancelled to settle personal matters. Also, if MOM asks us for extra documents during the process, how do we send those in? And one more thing — after cancellation, if the person still has their physical EP card, what should we do with it?
expected_answer: You can submit the cancellation request up to 14 days in advance — so for a 15 February cancellation, you can submit from 1 February onwards. The cancellation is immediate unless it is an advance cancellation request. The employer or employment agent can submit the cancellation. Upon cancellation (or within a day after the EP expiration date), you can request a Short-Term Visit Pass (STVP) for the pass holder, which grants valid stay in Singapore for up to 90 days. If MOM emails you requesting more documents, you can submit them using the online form at https://form.gov.sg/#!/5f8d4eadef8dab00112fd313. Regarding the physical EP card, if the card is found (or still in possession), it should be cut in half and discarded to prevent misuse.

**Early Cancellation Submission**
You can submit the cancellation request **up to 14 days in advance**. Since the last day is 15 February, you can submit the request from 1 February onwards [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/cancel-a-pass.md].

**Allowing the Person to Stay After Cancellation**
When submitting the cancellation through the [EP eService](https://www.mom.gov.sg/eservices/services/employment-pass-eservice) on myMOM Portal, you can **request an STVP (Short-Term Visit Pass)** for the pass holder. This will grant them valid stay in Singapore for **up to 90 days** from the date of application. Both you and the pass holder will receive the STVP by email, which they'll need to show with their valid passport when leaving Singapore [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/cancel-a-pass.md].

**Important Note**: Once the EP is cancelled, the pass holder **cannot work**, even while waiting to leave Singapore [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/cancel-a-pass.md].

**Physical EP Card**
After cancellation, please **cut the card in half and discard it** to prevent misuse [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/cancel-a-pass.md].

(2) A 'Verified page' screenshot that must include the visible website address of the verification portal and the final page showing that the candidate was awarded the educational qualification. - Visible verification portal's website address (e.g., wis.ntu.edu.sg/webexe/owa/deg_verification.main)

question: I'm on an Employment Pass under the Sponsorship scheme and my pass still has about 4 months left. I want to renew early — will I lose those remaining months? Also, what form do I need to use, and what kind of obligations or commitments does the renewal involve regarding repatriation?
expected_answer: If you renew your Employment Pass early, your new work pass validity will not be reduced or lost. Any remaining validity from your current pass — up to six months — is added on to your renewal, so your 4 remaining months would carry over. As an EP (Sponsorship) holder, you must use the specific EP Sponsorship renewal form for your renewal application. The form requires the candidate's name as shown on their travel document, their signature, and the date in DD/MM/YYYY format. **You will NOT lose your remaining months by renewing early:**
- You can apply to renew **up to 3 months before** your pass expires [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/renew-a-pass/ep_sponsor_renewal_form.md].
- When you renew early, any remaining validity from your current pass (up to six months) is added on to your renewal — your new work pass validity will not be reduced or lost [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/renew-a-pass/index.md].

**Form required:**
- You must use the **Employment Pass (Sponsorship) Renewal Form** [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/renew-a-pass/index.md].

Your local sponsor must undertake to:

question: We have an ONE Pass holder whose spouse holds a Dependant's Pass and now wants to start her own business in Singapore. The DP currently has about 2 months of validity left. question: We're preparing an EP application for a candidate whose university doesn't appear in MOM's list of recognized institutions. On top of that, the candidate's nationality is already well-represented among our PMET staff, and I'm also wondering how our local PMET hiring ratio factors in. Can you walk me through what we need to handle for the qualification verification and how these workforce composition factors play into the application outcome?
expected_answer:
For the qualification verification: if the candidate's awarding institution cannot be found on MOM's list, you must enter its name exactly as it appears on the educational certificate, and the employer must upload a verification proof of the qualification to confirm it is genuine and from an accredited institution.

Regarding workforce composition factors under the COMPASS framework, two distinct criteria are relevant:

1. Nationality diversity criterion: This criterion awards more points to applications where the candidate's nationality forms a small share of the firm's PMET employees. A diverse mix of nationalities enriches firms with new ideas and networks and contributes to a more inclusive and resilient workforce. Since the candidate's nationality is already well-represented among your PMET staff, this criterion would award fewer points for the application.

2. Local PMET share criterion: Points are also affected by whether your firm has a relatively higher share of locals among PMET employees compared to your peers in the same sector. A higher local share relative to sector peers would be favorable.
actual_answer:
Based on the COMPASS framework, here's what you need to know:

## Qualification Verification

**If you need points from the qualifications criterion (C2)**, you must submit **verification proof** together with your candidate's qualifications when you apply for the EP [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]. Since the university isn't on the top-tier list, the candidate would earn **10 points** for holding a degree-equivalent qualification (versus 20 points for top-tier institutions) [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md].

**However**, if you don't need points from this criterion to reach the required 40 points, you don't need to submit the qualifications or verification proof at all [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md].

## Workforce Composition Impact

**Diversity (C3) - Nationality representation:**
Since the candidate's nationality is well-represented among your PMETs:
- If that nationality forms **25% or more** of your PMET workforce: **0 points**
- If it's **5% to less than 25%**: **10 points**
- If it's **less than 5%**: **20 points**

[source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]

**Support for Local Employment (C4) - Local PMET share:**
Your points depend on how your organization's local PMET share compares to your sector:
- **50th percentile and above**: **20 points**
- **20th to less than 50th percentile**: **10 points**
- **Below 20th percentile**: **0 points**

*Safety net*: If your local PMET share is at least 70%, you'll score at least 10 points regardless of sector comparison [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md].

You can check your exact scores using the **Workforce Insights tool** on myMOM Portal [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md].

question: I'm currently exploring my options between the ONE Pass and the Employment Pass. expected_answer: If you hold a ONE Pass (Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass), you do not need to reapply for a pass if you change jobs. In fact, the ONE Pass provides the flexibility to concurrently start, operate, and work for multiple companies at any one time (subject to your employment contract terms, where relevant). It is also exempt from the Complementarity Assessment Framework (COMPASS) and Fair Consideration Framework job advertising requirements. Additionally, passes are available for eligible family members, and your spouse will be able to apply to work on a Letter of Consent. You may also apply for the ONE Pass without meeting the salary criteria if you have outstanding achievements in at least one specified area. Separately, for Employment Pass holders who are still in Singapore after their pass is cancelled, they can request a Short-Term Visit Pass (STVP) to grant them a valid stay for up to 90 days from the date of application.

question: I'm renewing my Employment Pass and I want to understand what gets verified during the process. The results of the verification are then communicated by the Comptroller of Income Tax to the Controller of Work Passes.

Regarding educational qualification verification: if the institution name on the educational certificate or verification proof is not available in the dropdown menu, the applicant should enter the institution's most recent name where applicable. Alternatively, the applicant may choose not to declare the qualification if they are unable to find it on the list. - **Primary verification**: Your income is verified against your assessment record for the **current Year of Assessment**
- **Fallback method**: If your current Year of Assessment record isn't available or finalized yet, IRAS will verify against your assessment records for the **two previous Years of Assessment**

question: I'm applying for an Employment Pass and trying to understand the COMPASS bonus points. My company is wondering if we can get bonus points — we might qualify under the Shortage Occupation List for the C5 skills bonus, and we're also looking at the C6 SEP bonus. What do we need to do on both fronts to be eligible for these bonuses?
expected_answer: For the C5 Skills bonus (Shortage Occupation List), applicants should select one of the eligible job titles in the EP application form. This job title must be the same as the occupation used for the job advertisement in MyCareersFuture (MCF), unless the employer is exempted from the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) job advertising requirement. For the C6 Strategic Economic Priorities (SEP) bonus, the organisation needs to participate in at least one of the eligible programmes. Specifically, firms must be supported by economic agencies or NTUC, and must participate in or meet the criteria for at least one of the specified programmes/categories to be considered for the SEP bonus.
actual_answer:
Based on the knowledge base, here's what you need to do to be eligible for each bonus:

## C5. Skills Bonus (Shortage Occupation List)

To obtain the **20 points** for C5:

- **Your candidate must perform the job duties** listed for the specific shortage occupation on the SOL [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/compass-c5-skills-bonus-shortage-occupation-list-sol/index.md]
- **Select the shortage occupation** in your EP application [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]
- **Meet additional requirements** as stated in the SOL Employer Guide — MOM will check the candidate's job duties, past work experience, and qualifications or industry accreditation [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]

**Important note:** If your candidate needs the SOL bonus points to pass COMPASS, they can **only work in that specific shortage occupation**. Redeploying them to a different job requires notifying MOM for reassessment [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md].

Note: You may receive only **10 points** instead of 20 if the candidate's nationality already forms 1/3 or more of your organization's PMETs [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md].

## C6. Strategic Economic Priorities (SEP) Bonus

To obtain the **10 points** for C6:

- **Participate in or meet criteria** for at least one eligible programme run by supporting sector agencies [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]
- **Contact the relevant sector agency** to understand qualifying criteria for the various programmes [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/compass-booklet.md]
- The award is **at the discretion of the supporting agencies**, and MOM will notify you if approved [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]

question: We're putting together an EP application and trying to understand how COMPASS scoring works. Our candidate scores well on salary and qualifications but we're not sure about the firm-level criteria. Can you explain how the COMPASS points are structured — like what categories feed into the overall score and how they're grouped?
expected_answer: COMPASS requires an application to earn at least 40 points to pass. The points are structured into two groups: an "Individual score" and a "Firm-Related score." The Individual score is based on candidate-specific criteria — C1 (Salary) and C2 (Qualifications) — while the Firm-Related score is based on the employer's workforce profile — C3 (Diversity) and C4 (Support for Local Employment). Each of these four foundational criteria can award 0, 10, or 20 points. In addition, there are two bonus criteria: C5 (Skills Bonus for Shortage Occupation List, worth up to 20 points) and C6 (Strategic Economic Priorities Bonus, worth 10 points). The total across all criteria must reach at least 40 points for the application to pass COMPASS.
actual_answer:
Based on the knowledge base, COMPASS uses **6 criteria** organized into two main groups:

## **Foundational Criteria** (4 criteria, up to 20 points each):

- **C1 - Salary**: Benchmarks the candidate's salary against local PMET salaries in your sector [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]
- **C2 - Qualifications**: Awards points based on the candidate's educational qualifications [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]
- **C3 - Diversity**: Awards points when the candidate's nationality forms a small share of your firm's PMET employees [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]
- **C4 - Support for Local Employment**: Based on your local PMET share relative to industry peers [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]

## **Bonus Criteria** (2 criteria):

- **C5 - Skills Bonus**: Up to 20 points for candidates in jobs where skills shortages exist [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index-compass.png]
- **C6 - Strategic Economic Priorities Bonus**: Up to 10 points for partnership with Government on investment, innovation, internationalization, or transformation activities [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index-compass.png]

**You need 40 points total to pass COMPASS** [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/eligibility/index.md]. C1 and C2 are individual attributes, while C3 and C4 are the firm-level criteria you mentioned.

question: We're preparing a Letter of Consent application for a common-law spouse holding an LTVP under an ONE Pass holder. The applicant will be partially paid by both a local and an overseas employer. When filling in the salary section of the LOC form, how exactly does MOM define 'fixed monthly salary', and what happens if the fixed monthly salary amount we declare is higher than the basic monthly salary?
expected_answer: According to the LOC (Common-Law Spouse) Application Form, fixed monthly salary is defined as basic monthly salary plus fixed monthly allowances. For example, S$5,000 fixed monthly salary = S$4,500 basic monthly salary + S$500 fixed monthly allowances. MOM will use the fixed monthly salary to assess the application. If the amount indicated as fixed monthly salary is more than the basic monthly salary, MOM will take the difference as the 'fixed monthly allowances'. If there are no fixed monthly allowances, the amount of fixed monthly salary should be exactly the same as the basic monthly salary. For the salary payable by, there are three options: 'Local' (paid by a Singapore-registered employer or paid by an overseas employer which is then charged fully to a Singapore-registered employer), 'Overseas' (employer is not registered in Singapore or is a representative office registered with Enterprise Singapore), or 'Both local and overseas' (partially paid by both local and overseas employer).

Based on the knowledge base, here's how to handle the salary section for your Letter of Consent application:

## Definition of Fixed Monthly Salary

**Fixed monthly salary** is defined as the sum of:
- **Basic monthly salary** + **Fixed monthly allowances**

Where:
- **Basic monthly salary** = all remuneration payable monthly that does not vary from month to month on any basis, in respect of work done under the contract of service
- **Fixed monthly allowances** = all allowances payable monthly that do not vary from month to month on any basis

[source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-worker/sector-specific-rules/higher-skilled-workers-for-construction-sector/faqs-for-marketbased-skills-recognition-framework-construction-210214.md]

## What Happens if Fixed Monthly Salary Exceeds Basic Monthly Salary

If the fixed monthly salary amount you declare is **more than** the basic monthly salary:
- **MOM will take the difference as 'fixed monthly allowances'**
- MOM will use the fixed monthly salary to assess the application

**Important note:** If there are no fixed monthly allowances, the amount of fixed monthly salary should be exactly the same as the basic monthly salary. ## Definition of Fixed Monthly Salary

**Fixed monthly salary** is defined as the sum of:
- **Basic monthly salary** + **Fixed monthly allowances**

Where:
- **Basic monthly salary** = all remuneration payable monthly that does not vary from month to month on any basis, in respect of work done under the contract of service
- **Fixed monthly allowances** = all allowances payable monthly that do not vary from month to month on any basis

## What Happens if Fixed Monthly Salary Exceeds Basic Monthly Salary

If the fixed monthly salary amount you declare is **more than** the basic monthly salary:
- **MOM will take the difference as 'fixed monthly allowances'**
- MOM will use the fixed monthly salary to assess the application

**Important note:** If there are no fixed monthly allowances, the amount of fixed monthly salary should be exactly the same as the basic monthly salary. [source: www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/overseas-networks-expertise-pass/passes-for-families/long-term-visit-pass-for-overseas-networks-expertise-pass/working-in-singapore/loc_cls_application_form.md]

Make sure your declarations accurately reflect what's specified in the employment contract, as false declarations are an offence.
